summary: High packet loss: 66.3% dropped at SPAN destination (2.97 Gbps mirrored into 1 Gbps port) plus 3.34% dropped at SIEM NIC. SIEM receives only ~33.7% of intended traffic, severely degraded detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: SPAN oversubscription at DC-CORE-1 Gi1/0/48: SPAN session from DC-CORE-1 Gi1/0/1 should copy 55,631,220 packets (2.97 Gbps) but destination port is only 1 Gbps. Switch discarded 36,881,220 packets on output (66.30% lost, average load 100% of 1 Gbps, bursts higher). Additional bottleneck at SIEM eth1 which discarded 625,920 packets it did receive (3.34% lost) because capture interface cannot keep up.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM receives only 18,750,000 of 55,631,220 packets (~33.7%). ~66% blind spot for correlation/alerting; plus 3.34% additional loss at tool NIC causes incomplete events/flows and missed detections. Effective visibility for SIEM is severely degraded.

recommended_fix.why: SPAN drops packets when mirrored rate exceeds destination rate and has no buffering. TAP provides lossless copy. A packet broker after TAP can filter/slice (SIEM needs_full_payload=false, needs_both_directions=false) to reduce 2.97 Gbps to <1 Gbps to fit SIEM 1G port and eliminate both switch and tool drops.
